judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) rather than the parsed token object, and this code persists that envelope directly as the credential key. On any install with credential sharing off, the first Google token refresh stores {success:true, data:{...}} as credential.key; the next getGoogleAuth runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), fails because access_token/refresh_token now sit one level deeper, and every Google Calendar operation throws until the user manually reconnects the app.

On any install with credential sharing off, the first Google token refresh stores {success:true, data:{...}} as credential.key; the next getGoogleAuth runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), fails because access_token/refresh_token now sit one level deeper, and every Google Calendar operation throws until the user manually reconnects the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope), not the parsed token payload. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That stores the envelope as `credential.key` instead of the credential object shape expected by `googleCredentialSchema` (previously it stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`), so subsequent reads/parses of `credential.key` as a credential payload would break due to fields being nested under `.data`.
